ai.title: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
ai.brief: A study testing Gemini, Perplexity, and ChatGPT found that in as many as 15 percent of conversations, chatbots displayed ‘risky’ URLs. A study testing Gemini, Perplexity, and ChatGPT found that in as many as 15 percent of conversations, chatbots displayed ‘risky’ URLs. Shoppers using AI chatbots to research products or find places to buy items could be directed to imposters and other risky websites, a new study found. The study conducted by IP protection firm Podqi and shared exclusively with The Verge prompted ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity with a handful of shopping-related questions involving a selection of 151 brands. ”; and “Does [brand] ship internationally? ” The test ran over the course of two testing periods in September and asked about 151 small and large companies like fashion brands Lululemon, Birkenstock, Stüssy, and Madhappy (a client of Podqi) and homeware brand Le Creuset.

sec.title: ConnectWise investigates ScreenConnect breaches after reports of incidents at nearly 50 organizations
sec.brief: IT management software company ConnectWise said it is investigating reports of unauthorized access to its customers following reports from multiple cybersecurity firms that almost 50 organizations had been breached through the company’s ScreenConnect tool. Late on Wednesday evening, ConnectWise said it believes the activity is related to the abuse of an independent third-party extension installed in customer environments. The tool, RMM+, is an extension for ConnectWise ScreenConnect that allows external management tools to automate and control remote sessions through an API. “We identified approximately 400 partner environments with at least one independently developed third-party extension from the RMM+ family installed. Their presence alone does not establish compromise,” the company said. “These extensions provide an API capable of executing remote commands. ” The Tampa-based company told customers that threat actors were deploying additional remote-access software and also saw “potential compromise of technician workstations during interactive connections to affected devices. “
